Kim,

We still want to proceed — the product team is ready to start canary tests — but procurement needs the SOC2 snapshot and a clarified acceptance checklist to justify an exception.

Can you send an updated MAP with a proposed new close window and a compacted eval plan (2-3 day canary + 48h stability)? If not possible, we need an exec-level extension to the close date.

Thanks,

Orchid Analytics

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-06-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal procurement timing – ask to extend MAP runway

Emma —

Thanks for the heads up. Ive started a quick rebaseline of the MAP and the evaluation plan (attached). High-level proposal:
- Move contractual close from 2026-06-25 to 2026-07-09 (two-week extension) to accommodate procurement + PO timing.
- Condense technical evaluation into: 48h canary (1% traffic), 48h stress run (feature-complete test harness), 24h stabilization. Total gated window: 5 days.
- Add acceptance checklist items procurement requested (SOC2 artifact, KV retention policy note, audit-log sampling).

Were flagging three primary risks in the attached risk ledger:
1) Procurement PO delay (probable) — mitigation: exec extension + interim credit for late PO?
2) Integration test flakiness on customer dataset (medium) — mitigation: pre-canary synthetic run and stricter gating thresholds.
3) Performance variance at long-seq (low/unknown) — mitigation: run our quantized model variant during canary.

Grace / Rishi — can you confirm the condensed eval gates are technically sound and that we can produce the SOC2 snapshot by EOD tomorrow? Ill draft the exec escalation note if we need sign-off.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Orchid_MAP_v2.xlsx, eval-gating-criteria.md
From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>

Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Emma Cho <emma.cho@orchid-analytics.com>
Date: 2026-06-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Re: Internal procurement timing – ask to extend MAP runway

Kimberly / Emma —

I reviewed the condensed gating in the attached markdown. Tech acceptance looks achievable if we do the following:
- Pre-canary synthetic run tonight to catch obvious regressions.
- Canary config: 1% production-like traffic routed to dedicated dedicated pool with quantized variant; key metrics: 95p latency, error-rate < 1%, token-cost within 15% of baseline.
- Stress run: three scripted load profiles (baseline, burst x3, long-seq) over 48h.
- Rollback triggers: 30m sustained error rate > 1.5% OR 5% degradation in 95p latency.

Open items:
- We need a signed commitment on the data retention SLA from Orchid to enable KV caching during canary (cache invalidation risk otherwise).
- SOC2 snapshot: Rishi, can ops provide the redacted artifact and a one-page attest by tomorrow EOD?

If procurement cant meet 6/18 PO timing, well need the extension to 7/9. I think exec sign-off will be straightforward if procurement agrees to a short interim credit and the SOC2 artifact is delivered.

Grace O'Connor
Principal Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Team —

Summary: Orchid Analytics (ORCH-2026-145) cannot submit PO until 2026-06-18, pushing our planned close (6/25) into a high-risk state. Procurement has requested SOC2 snapshot and a short interim credit to rationalize the delayed PO internally. Technical team validated a condensed eval plan that preserves safety gates (see gating doc).

Request: approval for the following items so we can keep momentum and avoid losing timeline-driven pricing concessions:
1) Formal close-date extension to 2026-07-09 (two-week extension from current contract target).
2) A one-time onboarding credit of $7,500 to cover procurement approval friction (applied to first invoice).
3) Authorization to provide a redacted SOC2 snapshot and a one-page operations attest to Orchid by EOD 6/04.

Risk notes (short):
- Procurement PO delay (high probability) — impact: 2-week slip and potential pricing review.
- Customer-required data-retention addendum (medium probability) — impact: small legal review that could add 48-72h.
- If exec declines credit, customer may insist on delaying canary until PO closes, adding 3–4 weeks of runway loss.

Attachments: SOC2_snapshot_2026-05.pdf, Orchid_MAP_v2.xlsx, eval-gating-criteria.md

Action items: please reply with APPROVE / REJECT / NEED MORE INFO by 2026-06-05 10:00 PT. If approve, Legal will draft the narrow addendum and Finance will bake the credit into the first invoice.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
